blocks.text:
The paper hit the porch at seven sharp
Same as every day, same old tune
Strange thing about the morning headlines
Says the world will end by noon

Coffee’s cooling on the counter
Paper folded by the door
Been writing letters to the editor
Since nineteen ninety-four

Mostly drainage on Maple Avenue
And the garbage truck alarm
Little town complaints and gripes
That never did much harm

But this morning feels peculiar
Like the sky’s about to bend
Heard a rumor through the wires
That the whole damn world might end

Some big rock above the ocean
With a lunchtime rendezvous
Funny thing about extinction
Is the silence around the news

I don’t mind the end of everything
If that’s the way it goes
But don’t you take my final morning
And close it up in prose

Let a man decide his last few hours
However they may be
With a cup of coffee cooling
And a letter signed by me

They say the vote was held in secret
Somewhere far across the sea
Deciding we were better off
Not knowing what would be

Guess they figured we’d go crazy
If we knew the clock was true
But I’d have liked a little longer
Just to think the whole thing through

Maybe pray or hug somebody
Maybe holler at the sky
Maybe sip a jar of moonshine
With the neighbors passing by

Instead I’m scratching ink on paper
Like I’ve done a thousand times
Funny how a small routine
Still steadies shaking minds

I don’t mind the end of everything
If that’s the way it goes
But don’t you take my final morning
And close it up in prose

Let a man decide his last few hours
However they may be
With a cup of coffee cooling
And a letter signed by me

Maybe papers burn by noon today
Blown through ash and flame
Maybe no one reads a single word
Written by my name

But if a soul finds one black page
Where these old thoughts remain
Tell ’em Terry Tuckwiggles
Still had something left to say

I don’t mind the end of everything
If that’s the way it goes
But don’t you take my final morning
And close it up in prose

Let a man decide his last few hours
However they may be
With a cup of coffee cooling
And a letter signed by me

notebook.style: piano-driven roots rock with a wry storytelling tone, 88–96 BPM, steady groove, Arrangement centered on rhythmic upright piano chords, electric bass, and a tight drum kit with dry snare and light cymbal work, Occasional restrained electric guitar fills and subtle organ pads for warmth, Vocal delivery gritty and soulful but controlled, slightly raspy with expressive phrasing and dynamic swells, Lines should feel conversational and observational, with dry humor underneath the emotion, Production warm and vintage: light tape saturation, close-miked piano, punchy bass, restrained room ambience, Avoid arena polish, Intro begins mid-groove as if the listener tuned into a late-night radio performance already in progress, Mood reflective, sardonic, and human—like a barroom storyteller calmly describing the end of the world with a weathered voice,
